steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Huff... huff...
The alley stretches on, giving Dove enough room to flee. But her strength is also fading, her pace slowing with each step.
Finally she collapses to the ground, gasping for air. You took the chance and block her escape route. Through your perseverance, the stubborn chase has finally ended in your favor.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Oh... oh, it's you! You almost scared me to death. I thought it was a ghost watching me through the back window...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I'm so sorry. I shouldn't have run like that, made you chase me so far... I've heard some ghost stories around lately, so I might have overreacted...

Surprisingly, Dove speaks up first, her attitude totally not what you expected. Her voice remains soft and gentle, as if your confrontation through the window and the subsequent chase were nothing but a misunderstanding.
As she speaks, she looks up at you with her shiny eyes. She sounds genuinely apologetic, yet obviously avoids mentioning the cause of all this—those letters she opened.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You did... overreact. But was it really the ghost stories? Or, perhaps it's because I saw what you were doing with those letters?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Letters? What... I don't know what you're... Oh, you mean those undelivered ones? Yeah I was processing them. That's my work.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Processing, you mean opening those private letters without permission?

Your voice is steady, making no haste to press further. Instead, you start catching up Dove's every single word. You know that just like in the previous chase, she will eventually lead herself to a dead end.
As you expected, upon hearing the words opening letters, her pupils constrict and face pales.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Is that something you've encountered before? I'll admit, sometimes I do replace envelopes before delivering letters...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: But that's only when one's damaged or tainted with blood. It would be unsightly... Other than that, I swear...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Oh? So that's why the letters you deliver look so pristine, almost as if they are... forged? Because you replace those envelopes?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And you did all this because it would be unsightly?
Your words hit the mark. Dove startles and lowers her head, as if trying to cover her face, or escaping your scrutiny.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I know it sounds foolish, but it's the best I can do to help them—because I'm a mere mail carrier.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A mere mail carrier? You're far more than that, Dove.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Didn't you forge letters to "fulfill" the townspeople's wishes? Like that letter from the head nurse, some "tolling the death knell" stuff?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I don't know how you mimic handwriting, or grasp information not mentioned in the letters... but I assume it has something to do with your special ability?
You keep a watchful eye on her every subtle reaction. Her clenched hands and paling face are betraying her. Still denying though, her voice sounds feeble.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I... I don't know what you're talking about!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright Dove, cards on the table. I'll go first: I'm an investigator from DisCity and I know enough about Sinners and their power, so don't try and fool me.
You step forward and grasp her wrist. A red light flashes, and the shackles connect you both. You're right. She is a Sinner.
Sensing this unusual connection, Dove jolts her head up and stares at you in shock. She's never expected such an extraordinary investigative technique from you.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: What is this...?! What did you do to me...?!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't be afraid. I'm here to investigate the Mania in Désir and uncover the truth. As long as you cooperate, I won't harm you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: From what I gather, the letters of the townspeople never actually leave Désir. You open them, using the information to craft those responses. That's why they all look pristine and come back so soon.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And you use them to deceive the townspeople, playing the role of a kind-hearted mail carrier, all to keep the hoax of Désir's unnatural, deceptive nature. Am I right?
Your pointed, blunt question seem to have touched the truth and stung Dove.

Her shoulders tremble, then suddenly she swings her head up, barely suppressing her anger and hatred. For a moment, you think she may lash out, but in the end, her face just falls into a look of pure hurt.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: No... that's enough! Why do you have to think the worst of me, of this town?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: We're not born in DisCity, and yes, we take stealthy ways to sneak in there... But everyone here is trying their best just to survive!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Yes, I am a Sinner, and yes, I forged the letters. Maybe you see that as an unforgivable crime...
Dove looks up at you, her eyes glistening with unshed tears. You can't quite tell if they are a sign of her distress, or some deeper pain out of long-standing grief and loss.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: But I really don't know anything about the Mania or any truth of this town! I did all this because...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Because I... I just want everyone to have a better life! That isn't a lie, at least...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your actions tell a different story.
Dove registers your skepticism, her fingers brushing away the tears, seemingly both composing herself and suppressing her emotions.
You stay on high alert in case she lashes out for failing her disguise. To your surprise, she just reaches into her messenger bag and produces several letters.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...What was that?!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: They're from those who've gone to DisCity... and the replies I've prepared.
Dove nervously gestures for you to take the letters. She glances around cautiously before continuing.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Many of them wrote to their families while waiting for their trips. So I made these replies... But some left all in a hurry, without saying goodbye to anyone.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: That's all I have. I hope they could be useful. Otherwise, I can't offer any other help, nor can I prove my innocence...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Take them if you want. I guess you'll not listen to me anyway.
You look into Dove's slightly petulant and aggrieved expression closely. After a moment's consideration, you decide to trust your shackles and your gut feeling.
You reach out and take the letters from Dove. The one on top is as light and thin as it appears. The sender's name on the envelope catches your eye—Sheila.
